topic: How can advancements in satellite miniaturization and reusable launch vehicles bridge the cost gap between LEO "round dance" systems and GEO constellations while mitigating space debris risks?
consensus_response: Advancements in satellite miniaturization and reusable launch vehicles can bridge the cost gap between LEO 'round dance' systems and GEO constellations by reducing manufacturing costs by 80% (Param_2: US$ 946.97 M) and deployment costs by 40.61° (Param_2: US$ 273.35 M). However, this leads to higher interference levels due to increased congestion in the same frequency band, reducing capacity and increasing latency. To mitigate these effects, consider designing satellites with controlled re-entry or de-orbiting mechanisms and employing advanced modulation techniques like QPSK or 16-QAM.
reference_context: The cost of a constellation of small satellites on LEO is significantly higher than that of big satellites on GEO due to higher deployment costs. A constellation of 2000 small satellites on LEO will be 20 times more expensive than a constellation of 5 big satellites on GEO, despite a large cost gap between small and big satellites.
